pairs.subject: conformance-checking
pairs.evidence: crates/store/src/conformance/mod.rs:58 The conformance suite executes domain checks returning a binary Result<()> that panics on failure rather than publishing structured findings across a finding severity ladder with declared deviations registered.

techniques.evidence: crates/store/src/conformance/mod.rs:57 The suite collapses all evaluation into panicking on assertion failure rather than categorizing observations into hard failures, failures, warnings, and unable-to-check outcomes.

crates/store/src/conformance/events.rs:122 Discrepancies in Postgres and Firestore default behaviors are documented in doc comments rather than recorded in an enumerable declared deviation register containing document, clause, cost-motivation, and reconciliation state.
crates/store/src/conformance/events.rs:19 Assertions verify execution without tagging proofs by rung (presence, shape, execution) or emitting remediation details alongside findings.

crates/store/src/conformance/catalog.rs:206 The suite actively guards against false passes by ensuring that omitted difficulty levels remain unassigned instead of being silently coerced into an intermediate tier.
crates/store/src/conformance/mod.rs:59 Successful test executions are never written back as proof stamps into the backend manifest or repository contract; proofs expire with the process.
crates/store/src/conformance/rollup.rs:19 The conformance tests return Result<()> with no weighted pass ratio, summary percentage, or runnable predicate metadata.

crates/store/src/conformance/fixtures.rs:12 Precondition does not hold: the suite tests in-memory data structures and backend stores using entity fixtures rather than evaluating whole fixture repositories.
crates/store/src/conformance/events.rs:14 Precondition does not hold: checks are implemented directly in Rust rather than inferred from inline execution commands embedded in a specification format.
crates/store/src/conformance/scores.rs:11 Precondition does not hold: the conformance suite is developed and versioned in-tree without tracking external specification editions.
crates/store/src/conformance/alerts.rs:20 Precondition does not hold: the harness exercises backend domain methods rather than enumerating an independent rule registry with fail/pass fixtures.

crates/store/src/conformance/events.rs:59 Precondition does not hold: test expectations are fixed values derived from test inputs rather than dynamically computed from an untyped target without fixtures.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard defines conformance checking around programs that evaluate a repository against a contract, but internal subsystem harnesses (such as backend-agnostic storage trait suites) face identical hazards around silent false passes, unstratified deviations, and uncalibrated severity; the standard should explicitly address in-process trait/API contract checkers.

pairs.subject: conformance-checking
pairs.evidence: crates/store/src/conformance/driver.rs:26 The conformance driver executes sections or refusal walks directly to panic on assertion failure without publishing structured findings, classifying outcomes across a finding severity ladder, or recording deliberate non-conformance in a declared deviation register.

techniques.evidence: crates/store/src/conformance/admission.rs:242 Non-atomic admission on Firestore is printed to stderr rather than emitted as a warning or deferred outcome on a structured severity ladder.

crates/store/src/conformance/admission.rs:251 Deliberate backend non-conformance (non-atomic admission on Firestore) is branched ad-hoc in test code rather than registered in an enumerable declared deviation register.
crates/store/src/conformance/driver.rs:27 The driver runs execution tests without annotating findings by proof rung (presence, shape, execution) or reporting actionable remediation on failure.
crates/store/src/conformance/admission.rs:271 The test harness validates negative controls against non-atomic implementations to prevent false-pass certifications of race-prone stores.
crates/store/src/conformance/driver.rs:36 Successful conformance execution does not write proof back into any contract or capability manifest; evidence disappears upon process termination.
crates/store/src/conformance/driver.rs:18 The harness emits no pass ratio, score percentage, or predicate breakdown, reducing the conformance assessment to an all-or-nothing Result.

crates/store/src/conformance/driver.rs:19 Precondition does not hold: the conformance driver executes against in-memory or database trait implementations rather than judging committed whole repository trees.
crates/store/src/conformance/driver.rs:25 Precondition does not hold: checks are declared as Rust code methods rather than inline shell command predicates within a specification sheet.
crates/store/src/conformance/driver.rs:40 Precondition does not hold: the suite is maintained internally without numbered specification editions or upstream suite revisions to stratify.

crates/store/src/conformance/refusals.rs:40 Precondition does not hold: the conformance harness checks trait methods rather than an independent registry of linter or gate rules with paired fail/pass fixtures.

crates/store/src/conformance/refusals.rs:81 Precondition does not hold: expected methods are looked up from static SURFACE_METHODS metadata rather than derived dynamically from the codebase under test without fixtures.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard's definition of declared-deviation registers should provide guidance on how runtime capabilities matrices (such as Capabilities declarations) can fulfill or integrate with deviation registration.
